disposition_summary: One candidate mechanism submitted (CAND-1: a Hasse-Weil/Tate-isogeny-theorem closure showing that embedding a target elliptic curve as a Poincare factor of any genus-g>=2 curve's Jacobian, then attacking it via the best published genus-g hyperelliptic/plane-curve index calculus, costs Otilde(N^{2-2/g}) >= Otilde(N^1) -- strictly worse than direct Pollard rho at Otilde(N^{1/2}) for every g -- an unconditional, zero-heuristic closure of that specific attack family, with a full proof_search_map, an explicit forward-guidance open question (a factor-restricted/relative index-calculus variant, F3), and an honest priority of 'medium' rather than 'high' because it forecloses rather than advances a path to beating rho. Six candidate objects were considered in total (OBJ-1 through OBJ-6); five were rejected at the applicability-check or lossy-projection-test stage before a full candidate record was written, each with a named, checked reason recorded in source-novelty-audit.yaml's rejected_sketches, including one case (Smith 2008 genus-3 transfer) where an initial recollection was deliberately checked by WebFetch and found wrong before being discarded rather than being silently dropped.
